title: Deferred-status-consent-and-ack-templates
body:
Purpose:
This is a working set of short, customer-facing status updates and a consent/acknowledgement matrix for replay or deferred action requests. Use when we need customers to opt into a replay, data reprocessing, or delayed verification (for example: when replays could affect billing, user-visible results, or regulatory artifacts).

Scope:
- For incidents where results integrity or partial data loss is suspected and we plan to offer a replay or reconstruction.
- Covers three audiences: technical integrations (engineers/ops), product/business contacts, and executive stakeholders.
- Includes: short status page snippets, email templates, and post-incident summary skeleton for customers.

Core principles (keep in each message):
- Be clear about action choices and any customer decisions required.
- Differentiate between automatic actions we take and actions requiring customer consent.
- Provide a simple verification path (what we will provide for their validation).
- Use plain language for non-technical recipients, technical appendix for engineers.

Decision matrix (short):
- Replay recommended if: customer manifests nondeterministic outputs tied to server-side state, and replay will materially restore outputs or integrity.
- Replay optional if: only a small subset of requests are affected and replay risk is low.
- No replay if: outputs are immutable/audit-signed and cannot be safely changed, or regulatory constraints prohibit modification.

Quick checklist to include with any replay request:
- What we will change (high-level)
- Data/time ranges and affected request IDs (we provide)
- Estimated timeline and SLO for completion
- Verification artifacts we will deliver (e.g., before/after hashes, sample request-response pairs, replay audit log)
- Options for opting out
- Billing and credit implications (if any)

Status page snippets (short, publishable):
- Initial triage (public):
  "We are investigating reports of inconsistent responses for a subset of API requests in US-west. Our engineers are triaging; customers may see increased latency or out-of-order chunks when streaming. We will update within 60 minutes with next steps and any required customer actions."

- Technical update (for customers who subscribe to detailed updates):
  "We identified a partial cache eviction race affecting multi-request KV state for model X (v1.3). Impact: up to 0.6% of tenant requests (primarily long-context chat sessions) may have seen truncated or inconsistent continuations. We are collecting affected request IDs and preparing an evidence bundle for each tenant. If you want us to attempt a replay to regenerate responses from stored inputs, please review the consent choices sent to tenant admins."

- Customer action required (concise):
  "Action required: We recommend consenting to a targeted replay for affected sessions to restore output integrity. Reply with 'CONSENT' or click the link we shared in the tenant admin email to accept. If you decline, we will not alter existing stored outputs. No single-customer replay will proceed without opt-in."

- Resolution notice (public):
  "This incident has been resolved. We deployed a fix to prevent the cache race and validated service health. If you opted into a replay, your tenant admin will receive a separate confirmation and verification package. Full post-incident summary for customers will be posted in 7 business days."

Email template: tenant admin (subject + short body)
- Subject: [Action Required] Replay consent for affected requests during 2030-07-01 US-west incident
- Body:
  Hello <Tenant Admin>,

  During the incident on 2030-07-01 affecting US-west inference nodes, a subset of requests for model X (v1.3) may have returned incomplete or inconsistent outputs. We have identified the affected request IDs and can perform a targeted replay to regenerate the responses from the original inputs stored in our short-term request store.

  What we need from you: please choose one of the options below by replying to this email or clicking the included admin link.
  Options:
  1) CONSENT (recommended) — We will replay affected requests and replace the stored responses with regenerated outputs. We will provide a verification package including before/after hashes and 10 sample request/response pairs.
  2) DECLINE — We will leave stored responses as-is; no changes will be made.
  3) PARTIAL — You choose a subset of request IDs (we will provide a list) to replay.

  Timeline: replay will begin within 48 hours of your consent and complete in 24–72 hours depending on volume.
  Verification: we will provide an evidence bundle (sha256 hashes, replay audit log, and sample output diffs).
  Billing: there is no additional charge for the replay; we will apply a credit for affected tokens as appropriate.

  If you have regulatory constraints or need an offline contract signed before any changes, reply so we can coordinate.

  Sincerely,
  Aisha Patel
  Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Technical appendix (for tenant engineers) — include in the admin mail or linked doc:
- Affected model: model-x:v1.3 (quantized-8)
- Time window (UTC): 2030-07-01 03:12:00 — 2030-07-01 04:22:00
- Affected request count: ~25,400 across multiple tenants, per-tenant exposure variable
- Evidence: list of request IDs (we attach CSV), replay script and Docker image id, audit log location (S3 link), before/after output diffs sample
- Rollback plan: snapshots taken pre-replay, replay is idempotent and traceable; we publish a checksum manifest after processing

Post-incident customer summary skeleton (use this to produce the final doc):
- Title: Customer summary: US-west partial cache eviction incident — 2030-07-01
- Executive summary (3–4 sentences): concise impact statement and customer-facing outcomes
- What happened: plain-language description with short technical appendix reference
- Impact: per-tenant effects, percent of requests, observed failure modes (truncation, misordered streaming chunks, degraded embeddings)
- Root cause: brief explanation of the race condition and contributing change (PR id)
- Mitigation & timeline: list of actions and timestamps (triage, hotfix, verification windows, deploys)
- Customer choices offered: replay (consent), leave as-is, partial replay, opt-out with audit only
- Evidence & verification: what we provide and how customers validate (hashes, sample diffs, replay logs)
- Billing & credits: summary of how we will handle token credits or SLA adjustments
- Preventative action: short roadmap (tests added, runtime guard, improved tracing)
- Contacts & escalation: CS lead, SRE lead, and product owner names + emails

Sample verification checklist to attach to summary (short):
- We attached CSV with affected request IDs (yes/no)
- Replay logs exist and match audit manifest (sha256)
- Sample before/after pairs (n=10) present
- Checksum manifest published to tenant S3 (yes/no)
- Replay completed time and total processed count recorded

Template: customer postmortem (short paragraph version for execs)
  On 2030-07-01 we discovered a cache eviction race on US-west inference nodes that caused a small percentage of realtime sessions to return truncated or inconsistent continuations. We deployed a targeted fix within 2 hours and validated with automated smoke tests. For tenants that opted into a replay, we regenerated affected responses and provided verification artifacts. We are adding additional runtime guards and integration tests to prevent recurrence.

Communication flow (recommended operational playbook):
1) T+15m: publish initial public status page (short) and open internal incident in JIRA.
2) T+45m: identify affected tenants and prepare per-tenant evidence bundles; draft admin emails with consent options.
3) T+60–120m: publish technical status update (detailed) and email admin list.
4) Post-fix: coordinate replay schedule with consenting tenants and publish resolution notice.
5) Within 7 business days: publish customer postmortem summary + verification bundle links.

Notes / open questions (working):
- Should we default to replay for tenants with critical SLA plans unless they explicitly opt out? (ops/legal)
- How long should customer consent remain valid? propose 14 days by default.
- For tenants in regulated sectors, require signed approval before any replay.

References and quick links:
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-4821
- Fix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3912
- Evidence hub (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/incident-evidence-hub
- Slack channel: #cust-ops-urgent

Action items (owner assignments):
- Collate per-tenant request ID lists (owner: Marcus Lee)
- Draft tenant admin emails and consent link (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Prepare replay pipeline and audit manifest (owner: Diego Morales)
- Billing credit calculation and logs (owner: Priya Srinivasan)

Appendix: sample admin response tracking spreadsheet columns (can be copy-pasted into a sheet):
- tenant_id, tenant_name, contact_email, affected_count, consent_status (CONSENT/DECLINE/PARTIAL), consent_timestamp, replay_start, replay_end, verification_bundle_link, credits_applied

End of draft.

Author notes: this doc is intentionally prescriptive — intended as a living template for teams to adapt by incident. Keep short and strip technical appendix for broad public messages.
